topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics welcome the class, recap foundational concepts of cancer progression, and outline the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer evolution and microenvironments.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Drivers of Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how somatic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective growth advantages that drive clonal tumor progression.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue hierarchies and stemness properties determine which cell types can initiate and propagate malignancies.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Triggers of Tumor Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how inflammatory signals and supportive stromal interactions provide the non-mutational environment necessary for malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Experimental and Spatial Technologies for Profiling Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the experimental, single-cell, and spatial omics technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and cell-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Integrative Framework of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the combined evolutionary contributions of cell of origin, mutational accumulation, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental factors in cancer development.

topics.label: Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
